name: Timers
description: Time logs against tasks: server-enforced start/stop (62 — Timer) over an is_running/duration_seconds pair, at most one running timer per owner. No page object — generated UIs (Scroll) manage time logs from the schema; start/stop/running are server routes (objects/site/timer_actions.py), not a generator page. Ships an attention provider for the `submitted` gate: approval is by design somebody other than the person who logged the hours, which makes it the kind of queue that can only be cleared by a person who has no reason to know it exists. The count carries hours in its detail, because nine entries and sixty-two hours are different amounts of afternoon. 0.5.0 gives the approval queue somewhere to go. "No page object" was true and also meant no page: the attention count pointed at /time-logs?status=submitted and nothing answered that path, so the one surface that could tell an approver a queue exists linked nowhere. This version keeps the no-page-object rule and satisfies it the way the rest of the box does -- a seeded `views` record over the generic `list` block and a site_routes row to site_view_render, which is data, not a page object -- so `nav_optional` is retired and the app finally declares a door. The list omits the search box because time_logs declares no `search` fields (a box that searches nothing is a lie about the collection), keeps Add because retroactive logging is ordinary and the schema was always meant to be form-managed, and does not link rows because no /time-logs/{id} permalink is seeded. The attention path drops its query string: the generic filter bar comes from the schema's views.filter_fields and reads nothing from the URL, so ?status=submitted would have promised a filtered queue and delivered the whole collection. Worth naming as a live gap rather than hiding: every generic edit affordance is owner-gated, so an approver can SEE the submitted rows here but still approves through the API, because a manager is by definition not the owner of the hours they are approving.
